explanation: The first relay carried a flame lit at Olympia all the way to Berlin for the 1936 Games. An Olympic flame had first burned at Amsterdam in 1928.

claims.text: The Olympic torch relay was first held for the 1936 Berlin Olympics and was not part of the ancient Olympic Games.
The 1936 relay carried a flame lit at Olympia in Greece to Berlin.
A flame first burned at a modern Olympic Games at Amsterdam in 1928.

evidence.restatement: The Olympia-to-host-city torch relay was introduced for the 1936 Berlin Games (Carl Diem's idea). The ancient Games had a sacred flame at Olympia but no relay.
The 1936 relay carried fire kindled at Olympia to Berlin.
A flame was lit in a tower at the 1928 Amsterdam Games, the first modern Games to have one.

issues.note: Ancient Greek festivals such as the Panathenaia did hold torch races, so a reader who knows that might read 'ancient Greek Games' broadly. The statement says the Olympic relay was 'handed down', and it was invented in 1936, so False stands.
